header.title: Open Frame Studio
header.heroAlt: Open Frame Studio: a double tilt-and-turn window in the 2D editor with its dimensions, the project's frames on the left and the properties on the right
header.label: Window frames
header.tagline: From frame drawing to cutting list and IFC, in one free app
header.desc: Pick a template, divide the frame into bays and give each bay a door, sash, glass or panel. You see it in 3D straight away, together with the production lists and the Uw value.

meta.description: Free, open-source app for designing window and door frames in wood, aluminium and PVC: 2D editor with free layout, 3D view, production lists, Uw check and export to IFC, DXF, PDF and Excel. For Windows, macOS, Linux and the browser.
meta.title: Open Frame Studio — OpenAEC Foundation

layout.alt: Free layout of a door with side light: a door, a fixed-glass bay and a brick spandrel, with the buttons to split a bay and choose its infill on the left
layout.title: Divide the frame the way you want
layout.desc: Split a bay with a mullion or transom and choose a door, sash, fixed glass, panel or spandrel for each bay, with glazing bead and opening direction. Start from a door with side light, a door with transom light or a grid.

view3d.alt: 3D view of a front door with transom light, set in the brickwork
view3d.title: See the frame in the wall
view3d.desc: The 3D view follows your drawing: real profiles, glass in the rebate, sashes and doors as separate parts and the brickwork around them. You can check at a glance whether it is right.

production.alt: Production lists with the cutting list per part: profile, material, net and gross length and cutting angles, with tabs for glass, hardware, gaskets, panels, glazing beads and the parts list
production.title: The cutting list follows the drawing
production.desc: Every jamb, sill and sash member is in the cutting list, with net and gross length and cutting angle. There are also lists for glass, hardware, gaskets, panels and glazing beads. Joints follow joinery practice: mortise and tenon for wood, mitred for aluminium and PVC.

energy.alt: Energy overview with the average Uw value, the area and the transmission loss per frame, and a green OK per frame against the set limit
energy.title: Know straight away whether the Uw value fits
energy.desc: For each frame the app calculates the Uw value, the area and the transmission loss from the profiles and the glazing. Set a limit and see at once which frame meets it.

profiles.alt: Profile editor with the cross-section of a wooden frame profile with a double rebate, the profile library on the left and dimensions, rebate and Uf value on the right
profiles.title: Work with your own profiles
profiles.desc: Pick from the library of wood, aluminium, PVC and wood-aluminium, or draw a cross-section point by point. Set width, depth, rebate and Uf value, or import a profile from DXF.

notice.text: Early version (0.6). Try it and tell us what you miss.

features.label: Features
features.heading: Everything for the frame, from drawing to workshop
features.sub: Start with the highlights, or pick a topic.

editor.title: 2D frame editor
editor.desc: Columns and rows, drag handles and a closed chain of dimensions, with undo and redo.

templates.title: Templates
templates.desc: Tilt-and-turn, double, French window, top-hung, pivot, front door, sliding and lift-and-slide door. Save your own frame as a template.

infill.title: Free layout
infill.desc: Split, merge or swap bays and choose the infill, glazing bead, opening direction and hardware per bay.

shapes.title: Special shapes
shapes.desc: Segmental arch, round, trapezoid or an arch on sloping jambs, besides the usual rectangular frame.

view3d.title: 3D view
view3d.desc: Extruded profiles, glass in the rebate and the brickwork around it, also for stepped shapes such as a door with side light.

colors.title: RAL colours
colors.desc: A separate colour for the inside and outside, shown in 2D and 3D.

conventions.title: Dutch drawing conventions
conventions.desc: Dimensioning to NEN 3576 and opening symbols in the outside view to VKG and EN 12519.

library.title: Profile library
library.desc: Wood in standard KVT sizes (meranti, accoya, pine, oak, FSC hardwood), aluminium, PVC and wood-aluminium, with sash, door and glazing-bead profiles.

systems.title: Well-known systems
systems.desc: Templates for VEKA, Kömmerling, Reynaers CS 77 and Schüco AWS 75.SI+, among others, with mitred corners.

profileeditor.title: Profile editor
profileeditor.desc: Draw a cross-section point by point, with mirroring, snap grid and undo.

dxfprofile.title: Profile from DXF
dxfprofile.desc: Import a supplier's cross-section from a DXF file.

joints.title: Corner joints
joints.desc: Mortise and tenon, mitre, scribed or butt joint, set per corner. Your own choice always wins.

lists.title: Production lists
lists.desc: Cutting list with net and gross lengths and cutting angles, plus lists for glass, hardware, gaskets, panels, glazing beads and parts.

schedule.title: Frame schedule
schedule.desc: All frames with mark, dimensions, material, bays, glazing and Ug value. The desktop app turns it into a PDF or Excel file.

workshop.title: Workshop drawing
workshop.desc: A3 drawings with title block, and DXF with dimension lines for the workshop, from the desktop app.

uw.title: Uw per frame
uw.desc: Uw value, area and transmission loss per frame, checked against a limit you set yourself.

glazing.title: Glazing per bay
glazing.desc: Choose the glass per bay, such as double or triple glazing, with the Ug value that counts towards the Uw.

ifc.title: IFC export
ifc.desc: IFC 4 with the ILS Houten Kozijnen v2.0 property sets, for your BIM model. The desktop app also reads frames from IFC.

gltf.title: glTF and CSV
gltf.desc: The 3D model as glTF for visualisation, and the production data as CSV for your own software.

blender.title: Blender and Bonsai
blender.desc: Send a frame from the desktop app straight to Blender with Bonsai to continue modelling in IFC.

ai.title: AI assistant
ai.desc: Type "Make a tilt-and-turn 900×1400" and the frame appears. Works with OpenAI, Ollama or another compatible endpoint.

languages.title: Three languages
languages.desc: The app works in Dutch, English and German, with dimensions in millimetres.

themes.title: Light and dark
themes.desc: A light and a dark theme, in the style of the other OpenAEC apps.

download.title: Download v0.6.0
download.lead: Free, no account needed. For Windows, macOS and Linux.
download.browserNote: Rather not install anything? The app also runs in the browser.
download.label: Download
download.mobileNote: Open Frame Studio is made for a large screen. Open it on your computer, or try it here in the browser.

layout.title: Free layout
layout.desc: Click a bay for its infill, Ctrl+click for a mullion and drag the dividing lines.

view3d.title: 3D follows the model
view3d.desc: Stepped shapes, 45° mitres, glass in the rebate and sashes as real profiles.

cutting.title: Cutting list matches drawing
cutting.desc: Continuous mullions, spandrels and glass, sash, panel and glazing beads per bay.

joints.title: Joinery rules
joints.desc: Wood with tenoned jambs and continuous sills, aluminium and PVC mitred.

symbols.title: Opening symbols
symbols.desc: The outside view shows the opening and sliding direction to the Dutch convention.

saved.title: Settings are kept
saved.desc: Glazing bead, opening direction and hardware are kept after saving, switching and undo.

whatsnew.label: New in v0.6.0
whatsnew.title: Drawing, 3D and cutting list one to one
whatsnew.desc: In version 0.6 the free layout is the basis: what you draw is exactly what you get in 3D and in the cutting list.

files.a: Your own projects in .ofs. The desktop app also reads frames from an IFC file and profiles from DXF.

install.q: Do I need to install anything?
install.a: Not to try it out: the web version works right in the browser. To save and to export to IFC, DXF, PDF and Excel you need the desktop app; the browser cannot do that yet.

price.q: What does Open Frame Studio cost?
price.a: Nothing. The app is free and open source under the CC BY-SA 4.0 licence, with no account or subscription.

save.q: In which format is my work saved?
save.a: In its own .ofs project file. The desktop app also exports to IFC, DXF, PDF, Excel, CSV and glTF.

systems.q: Which systems does it run on?
systems.a: Windows (also without admin rights), macOS (Intel and Apple Silicon) and Linux (.deb, .rpm and AppImage), and in a modern browser.

practice.a: Yes. Dimensioning to NEN 3576, opening symbols to VKG and EN 12519, wood profiles in KVT sizes and IFC with the ILS Houten Kozijnen v2.0 property sets.

ai.q: What can an AI assistant do with it?
ai.a: The app has a built-in AI assistant that creates and edits frames from what you type. You connect it to OpenAI, Ollama or another compatible endpoint. There is no MCP server for external assistants yet.

curtainwall.q: Can I draw a curtain wall too?
curtainwall.a: In the desktop app, yes. The browser version cannot do that yet.

ready.q: Can I already order frames with it?
ready.a: It is an early version (0.6). Check dimensions and lists before you order or start cutting, and report errors on GitHub.

rust.title: Rust core
rust.desc: The data model, geometry and all exports (IFC, DXF, PDF, glTF, XLSX, CSV) live in one Rust library, with over a hundred tests.

tauri.desc: A thin native shell for Windows, macOS and Linux, with small installers.

svelte.desc: The same interface on the desktop and in the browser, with a 2D editor in SVG.

three.desc: The 3D view with extruded profiles and glass, right in the app.

wasm.desc: The Rust core runs as WebAssembly in the browser version.

ifc.desc: Open exchange with BIM software, following the Dutch ILS Houten Kozijnen v2.0.

tech.heading: Technology
tech.sub: For those who want to know how it is built.
